prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
It’s time for real change. After a decade of austerity and a rigged economy that rewards a privileged few, Labour will rebuild Britain so it works for the many, not the few—tackling the climate emergency, restoring living standards, and transforming public services.

- Green Industrial Revolution: Create 1 million unionised climate jobs; a £400bn National Transformation Fund (including £250bn Green Transformation Fund); a National and Regional Investment Bank network; rewrite Treasury rules so every pound spent aligns with climate goals. Delist companies that won’t act on the climate crisis and place a windfall tax on oil giants.

- Public ownership and lower bills: Bring rail, mail, water, energy and broadband into democratic public ownership. Deliver free full‑fibre broadband nationwide. Permanently ban fracking and expand community energy.

- Clean energy and homes: Aim for the substantial majority of emissions cuts by 2030; near-90% clean electricity by 2030; massive rollout of offshore/onshore wind, solar, new nuclear, storage and interconnectors. Upgrade almost all 27m homes to high efficiency; introduce a zero‑carbon homes standard; launch a Clean Air Act and a major programme of tree planting and flood defence.

- Work, pay and power: A Real Living Wage of at least £10 for all ages; day‑one rights, sectoral collective bargaining, ban zero‑hours and unpaid internships, end bogus self‑employment, strengthen unions and whistleblowing protections. Target a 32‑hour average full‑time week within a decade with no loss of pay. Inclusive Ownership Funds (up to 10% of large firms) to give workers a stake and dividends.

- Fair taxes and ending rip‑offs: Reverse Tory corporation tax cuts; ask only the top 5% (over £80k) to pay more income tax; no rises in VAT, NI or income tax for everyone else; toughest-ever crackdown on avoidance; 20:1 maximum pay ratios in the public sector; presumption to insource and take back PFI.

- NHS and care: End privatisation, restore capacity, invest 4.3% a year, free prescriptions and basic dentistry, free hospital parking, mental health on a par with physical health. Build a National Care Service with free personal care, end 15‑minute visits, better pay and training for care workers.

- Education for life: A National Education Service—Sure Start Plus; 30 free hours for all 2–4‑year‑olds; properly funded schools; scrap SATs; Arts Premium; bring academies/free schools under local oversight; free school meals for all primary pupils. Free lifelong learning up to Level 3; restore EMA; abolish tuition fees and reinstate maintenance grants.

- Homes and rights: Build over 1 million council and social homes in a decade; end Right to Buy; rent controls and open‑ended tenancies; end rough sleeping in five years; £1bn fire safety fund. Scrap Universal Credit, end sanctions and the hostile environment, end indefinite detention, and uphold equalities for women, BAME, disabled and LGBT+ people.

- Safer communities and justice: Rebuild neighbourhood policing and youth services; a public‑health approach to drugs; reunify probation; restore legal aid; tackle violence against women and girls.

- Democracy and devolution: Abolish the House of Lords for an elected Senate; votes at 16; automatic voter registration; ban dark money and paid second jobs; radical decentralisation with regional banks and local control.

- Brexit: Within six months, a legally binding final say between a new Labour deal (customs union, close Single Market alignment, rights and standards protected) and remain—implement the people’s choice.

- Internationalism with principle: Put human rights, peace and climate at the heart of foreign policy; War Powers Act; suspend arms sales where they fuel abuses (including Saudi in Yemen and where used to violate Palestinian human rights); recognise Palestine; maintain NATO, spend at least 2% on defence, renew Trident while pursuing disarmament. Keep DfID, 0.7% aid, and lead on climate justice.

For the many, not the few.
</text>
